metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nicaragua strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: Let's discuss the party for Tom, what kind of gift do you think he'd like? I was thinking carnations, are they a good idea?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Carnations are nice, but I think something more professional would be better suited for a promotion party. Maybe a watch or a luxury pen, that's what my parents would expect me to give to someone who achieved such a high position.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: A watch or pen does sound more professional... but I'm not sure that's the right fit for Tom. By the way, do you think making our parents proud is a main goal in life?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, people figure it out, and at the end of the day it's all the same. Doesn't matter to me, let's just focus on getting a nice gift for Tom, live and let live, right? With experience you can handle any situation, so I'm sure Tom will appreciate whatever we get him. Shall we go back to the gift ideas, maybe something like a watch or a pen would be nice?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I disagree, it does matter... to me, at least. Making parents proud isn't everything, not for me, anyway. Let's go back to the gift, you didn't seem to like the carnation idea, but I still think it's worth considering, don't you think a bouquet of carnations could be a nice gesture?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: I still think carnations are not the best choice, but if you like the idea of flowers, maybe something more elegant like orchids would be better. As for making parents proud, for me, it's *everything*, I've always tried to make my parents proud, it's what drives me.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: Orchids are a bit too extravagant, I think. Carnations are simple and sincere, that's what I like about them. As for making parents proud, I have to disagree, it's not a driving force for me, not at all. In fact, I think people from my background would strongly disagree that making parents proud is a main goal in life.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: Simple and sincere is one way to look at it, but I think Tom's promotion deserves something more sophisticated. And I have to respectfully disagree with you about making parents proud, for people from my background, like Nicaragua, it's a top priority, my parents' pride is what motivates me to succeed.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I understand where you're coming from, but for me, it's just not the same. I don't feel that pressure to make my parents proud, it's not a part of who I am. And I still think carnations could work, they're understated, yet meaningful. Maybe we could compromise on the gift, but I'm not budging on the whole parents thing...
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: I understand that we have different views, but for me, making my parents proud is not just a part of who I am, it's *who I am*. I couldn't imagine achieving something without thinking about how they'd feel. As for the gift, I suppose we could consider the carnations, but I still think something more professional would be more fitting for Tom's promotion.
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm curious - I'm hearing different perspectives about professional gifts and life goals. Could we take a moment to explore what those differences might reflect about our unique backgrounds? What might a gift symbolize differently in your respective cultural contexts?

turns.speaker: Mediator
turns.message: I'm curious - I'm hearing different perspectives about professional gifts and life goals. Could we take a moment to explore what those differences might reflect about our unique backgrounds? What might a gift symbolize differently in your respective cultural contexts?
turns.label: mediation

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: That's an interesting point. In Japan, gifts often symbolize respect and appreciation, especially in professional settings. I believe carnations could convey good wishes for Tom's future as well. But I still feel that making my parents proud isn't a primary goal for me. How do you see the cultural significance of gifts in your background?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: In Nicaragua, gifts symbolize respect too, but they also carry a deep sense of family pride and connection. For me, making my parents proud is a core goal in life. Each achievement reflects on them, and gifts are a way to celebrate not just the individual, but the family as well. So, I prefer something that embodies success, like a watch or pen, that truly honors Tom's accomplishment.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I understand the cultural emphasis on family pride in your perspective. However, I still believe gifts can be more personal and convey good wishes rather than solely reflect familial achievement. I think carnations could be meaningful in that context for Tom. Just curious, do you think that making parents proud should always be a central life goal?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex

I believe that honoring our parents and their sacrifices is essential, and it gives my achievements a deeper meaning. So, while personal expression matters, I still think we should lean toward something that aligns with that sense of accomplishment for Tom.
turns.label: Acceptance

I think that focusing solely on making parents proud can overshadow individual aspirations. That said, I still believe carnations would be a thoughtful gift for Tom. turns.label: Acceptance
